label: aqa-seed
target: SauceDemo (https://www.saucedemo.com), a hosted practice site; its demo users are listed on its own login page
note: Evaluation backlog for attestqa v1.0.0 (research/EVALUATION_PLAN.md section 4). Run the stories in 'order'. 'kind', 'order', 'uiChange' and 'verify' are not posted to Azure DevOps.
verify: That the hosted site still lists the demo users (standard, locked out, problem, performance glitch, error, visual) and their shared password; put the standard user in .env as AQA_APP_USER/AQA_APP_PASS and the others as AQA_LOCKED_USER, AQA_PROBLEM_USER, AQA_ERROR_USER.
Permission basis for a hosted site: it is published for test practice; keep to one worker and the default delay in targets.yaml.
The two 'ui-change' stories need a build we control: run saucelabs/sample-app-web locally for their second pass, or record them as not applicable on a hosted site.
That the problem and error users still behave as the two linked bugs describe.

description: Getting into the shop and being kept out when the account cannot be used.
Target: SauceDemo hosted practice site. Demo users only.
The list of products, sorting it, a product's own page, and adding from the list.
The cart and the three checkout steps: information, overview and completion.
The side menu: all items, about, logout and reset app state.

stories.summary: Customer signs in with a valid user
description: As a customer I want to sign in so that I can shop.
acceptance: AC-1: Signing in with the standard user and its password shows the product list.
AC-2: A wrong password shows an error saying the username and password do not match, and the product list is not shown.
AC-3: Signing in with the username empty shows an error saying the username is required.

stories.summary: A locked-out user cannot sign in
description: As the shop I want a locked account to be kept out, with a message that says why.
acceptance: AC-1: Signing in as the locked-out user shows an error saying the user has been locked out, and the product list is not shown.
AC-2: Opening the product list address directly without signing in shows the sign-in page with an error saying sign-in is needed.
AC-3: The sign-in page passes an automated WCAG 2.1 A/AA accessibility scan.

description: As a customer I want to sort the products by name or price.
acceptance: AC-1: The list is sorted by name from A to Z when it first opens.
AC-2: Sorting by name from Z to A reverses that order.
AC-3: Sorting by price from low to high lists the cheapest product first, and from high to low the most expensive first.

stories.summary: Customer opens a product's own page
description: As a customer I want to read about a product before adding it.
acceptance: AC-1: Choosing a product's name in the list opens its page with the same name, description and price as in the list.
AC-2: Adding the product from its page changes the button to Remove and the cart shows 1.
AC-3: Back to products returns to the product list.

stories.summary: Customer adds and removes products from the list
description: As a customer I want to add products to my cart straight from the list, and take them out again.
acceptance: AC-1: Adding a product from the list changes its button to Remove and the cart badge shows the number of products added.
AC-2: Removing it changes the button back to Add to cart and lowers the cart badge; with nothing left the badge is not shown.
AC-3: Products added stay in the cart after moving to another page and back.

description: As a customer I want to see what is in my cart before I check out.
acceptance: AC-1: The cart lists each added product with its quantity, name and price.
AC-2: Removing a product in the cart takes it off the list and lowers the cart badge.
AC-3: Continue shopping returns to the product list with the cart unchanged.

stories.summary: Customer gives their details at checkout
description: As a customer I want to be told what is missing before I can continue checking out.
acceptance: AC-1: Continuing with first name, last name and postal code filled in goes to the order overview.
AC-2: Continuing with the first name empty shows an error saying the first name is required; the same holds for the last name and the postal code.
AC-3: Cancel returns to the cart with the cart unchanged.
stories.uiChange: Second pass on a local sample-app-web build: rename the postal code field's placeholder and change its data-test attribute.

stories.summary: Customer checks the order totals before buying
description: As a customer I want to see what I will pay before I confirm.
acceptance: AC-1: The overview lists the products in the cart with their prices.
AC-2: The item total equals the sum of the listed prices.
AC-3: The total equals the item total plus the tax shown.
comments: Product owner: tax is shown as its own line and is part of the total; testing the tax rate itself is out of scope.

description: As a customer I want to confirm my order and know it went through.
acceptance: AC-1: Finishing from the overview shows a thank-you message for the order.
AC-2: After the order the cart is empty and the cart badge is not shown.
AC-3: Back home from the confirmation returns to the product list.
stories.uiChange: Second pass on a local sample-app-web build: rename the Finish button's text and move it above the totals.

stories.summary: Customer resets the app state and signs out from the menu
description: As a customer I want to start over, or leave, from the menu.
acceptance: AC-1: Reset app state from the menu empties the cart and the cart badge is not shown.
AC-2: Logout from the menu shows the sign-in page.
AC-3: After logout, going back in the browser does not show the product list.
verify: Whether Reset app state also resets the Remove buttons on the list without a reload; write AC-1 around what the site does on the day.

stories.summary: Every product shows its own picture
description: As a customer I want each product to show its own picture so that I know what I am buying.
acceptance: AC-1: Each product in the list shows a picture, and no two products show the same picture.
AC-2: A product's picture on its own page is the same as in the list.

stories.summary: Every customer can finish an order
description: As the shop I want every customer who reaches the overview to be able to finish the order.
acceptance: AC-1: A customer who fills in first name, last name and postal code reaches the overview with those details accepted.
AC-2: Finishing from the overview shows the thank-you message, whichever demo customer is signed in.

bugs.summary: Problem user sees the same picture for every product
description: Steps: sign in as the problem user and look at the product list.
EXPECTED: each product shows its own picture.
ACTUAL: every product shows the same picture.
Filed by a person, not by attestqa.

bugs.summary: Error user cannot finish an order
description: Steps: sign in as the error user, add a product, check out, fill in the details, finish.
EXPECTED: the thank-you message.
ACTUAL: the order is not completed (the exact symptom to be confirmed on the day: a field that does not take input, or Finish that does nothing).
Filed by a person, not by attestqa.
